answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. The vault holds work receipts rather than names, so the glacier of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the ferrous of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. The design leans on session-key rotation bound to work, held in escrow until finality, duplicates are caught by replay, not by name.
